rationale: C17 plausibly supplied a material event-greeting template: it marks a ceremonial opening, conveys congratulations despite the President's absence through a personal representative, interprets the event as symbolizing international aspirations, and closes by connecting the occasion to peace and freedom. The child follows a notably similar progression for the Mount Eisenhower dedication, while adapting it to Canadian-American friendship and shared wartime sacrifice. C14 shares the intermediary-conveyed congratulations and international-understanding theme but is shorter and less structurally complete. C22 also links greetings for an organized gathering, World War II service, freedom, and peace, but its labor-policy substance makes it a weaker template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Please give my personal greetings to everyone gathered there.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have asked my good friend and associate, Mr. Leonard W. Hall, to call upon Your Majesty as my personal representative and to convey to you my salutations and congratulations.
shared_material.explanation: Both use an intermediary or representative to convey presidential greetings at an international ceremonial event the President does not personally attend.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Congratulations to them for helping to advance the spirit of friendship which gives hope and strength to the building of peace.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I extend congratulations to your Nation... [and] express my personal hope that these great displays... will be a powerful force toward peace, freedom, and justice for all mankind.
shared_material.explanation: Both move from congratulations about the ceremony to a broader claim that the event advances international peace and freedom.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the mountain's name commemorated the victory of our allied forces... many men working together
shared_material.parent_excerpt: these great displays of the accomplishments and aspirations of the world's cultures
shared_material.explanation: Each interprets the commemorative object or exhibition as embodying cooperative international achievement rather than treating the occasion as merely ceremonial.
